The registry also carries latest and next; never write either into a recipe. Note the repo has TWO Dockerfiles and they are not interchangeable: docker/Dockerfile builds the published image by installing the released npm package, and the root Dockerfile builds the monorepo from source for contributors and is never published. You want neither, because the image already exists."
18	  - "⛔⛔ NOBODY BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR BY VISITING THE SITE, AND THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS. EverShop has NO admin signup route: the only admin pages in v2.2.1 are the login page, the login endpoint and the logout endpoint, and modules/auth/pages/admin/all/[context]auth.js redirects every other admin request straight to /admin/login when the session has no matching admin_user row. So an anonymous stranger CANNOT claim your store, which is unusual and good. The corollary is the part that bites: a fresh deploy has NO administrator at all and no way to create one from a browser. The admin account is created by a CLI call inside the container, at deploy time, and until you make it the shop has no owner. Do it as the last step of the deploy, before you hand over the URL."
19	  - "⛔ THE ADMIN-CREATION COMMAND EXITS 0 EVEN WHEN IT FAILED. bin/user/create.js catches every error and then calls process.exit(0), so a wrong password length, an unreachable database or a missing table all end in a green shell. NEVER treat the exit code as proof. Prove the outcome instead: POST the credentials to /admin/user/login and require HTTP 200 with a session id in the body. The verification script in this file does exactly that, and it is safe by construction because a 502 from the edge fails the login first."
20	  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST REACHES, BEFORE AND AFTER YOU CREATE THE ADMIN: the whole storefront, on purpose, because it is a shop. That includes GET / , the catalogue, the cart and the checkout, plus POST /api/customers, which is marked \"access\": \"public\" and is CUSTOMER registration, open by design and not admin registration. Everything under /admin is closed to anonymous requests, and every other /api route is private unless its own route.json says public (modules/auth/api/global/[getCurrentUser]auth.ts). Customer signup stays open after the first customer; there is no setting in v2.2.1 that closes it, so if the user needs a private store, put it behind something else rather than expecting a toggle."
21	  - "⛔ DATABASE: EverShop reads DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD as five separate variables (lib/postgres/connection.ts:9-14) and does NOT read a DATABASE_URL. deploy_compose only APPENDS redu's variables to the project .env, it never edits your compose, so the compose must map them itself: DB_HOST: ${PGHOST}, DB_PORT: ${PGPORT}, DB_NAME: ${PGDATABASE}, DB_USER: ${PGUSER}, DB_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}. There is NO SQLite fallback anywhere in the tree, so unlike most apps in this library a mis-wired database is loud rather than silent: the container fails on the first query. EverShop wants exactly ONE database, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule is satisfied and db_superuser is not needed."
22	  - "⛔ DB_SSLMODE MEANS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT libpq USERS EXPECT. In lib/postgres/connection.ts:18-56, require, prefer, verify-ca and verify-full all set rejectUnauthorized TRUE, i.e. the certificate IS verified, which is not what require means in libpq and is not what redu's managed Postgres presents. Leaving DB_SSLMODE unset gives ssl:false, which is the right answer over redu's private network: the app VM and the database VM are on the same private network and the database is not internet-reachable. If the user wants the connection encrypted anyway, the value is no-verify, NOT require. Say in the handover which one you chose."
23	  - "⛔ THE SESSION COOKIE SECRET DEFAULTS TO A PUBLICLY DOCUMENTED CONSTANT. getCookieSecret() returns the literal string \"keyboard cat\" when nothing is configured, and upstream's own configExample.text ships that same value, so every EverShop on the internet that skipped this step signs its session and cookie-parser cookies with a secret anyone can read. It is NOT an environment variable: it is the node-config key system.session.cookieSecret, so write it into a config file and mount it (this file shows how). Generate it once, keep it, and REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY: changing it signs out every admin and every logged-in customer at once. The session rows themselves live in the managed Postgres and survive."

25	  - "MOUNT A VOLUME ON /app/media OR EVERY PRODUCT IMAGE IS LOST ON THE NEXT REDEPLOY. lib/helpers.ts resolves MEDIAPATH to <cwd>/media and the image's working directory is /app, so uploads land on the container filesystem by default. This is the one people get wrong AFTER wiring the database correctly."

38	# Self-host EverShop on redu
39	
40	A real storefront with a real admin: catalogue, cart, checkout and orders, on one VM with a managed
41	Postgres beside it and a public HTTPS URL. About GBP 33 a month.
42	
43	## What this deploys
44	
45	- **EverShop** from the official image, pinned to `2.2.1`, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
46	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM: the catalogue, the orders and the customers.
47	- A volume on `/app/media`, which holds every product image you upload.
48	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
49	
50	About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.
51	
52	## Deploy
53	
54	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
55	directory containing this file:
56	
57	    Read redu.md and deploy EverShop on redu.
58	
59	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
60	
61	## The unusual thing about EverShop, and it is the important one
62	
63	**Nobody can claim your store by finding the URL.** EverShop has no admin signup page at all. The
64	only admin routes are the login page and the login endpoint, and everything else under `/admin`
65	redirects an unauthenticated visitor straight back to the login form.
66	
67	**The flip side is that a fresh deploy has no administrator whatsoever**, and no browser flow will
68	give you one. The admin account is created by a command inside the container, and until you run it
69	your shop has an open storefront and a locked back office you cannot enter.
70	
71	Worse, **the command exits 0 whether or not it worked**: its error handler prints the error and
72	then exits successfully. So the recipe below creates the account and then proves it by logging in.
73	
74	## The compose file
75	
76	One service. redu supplies the database.
77	
78	```yaml
79	services:
80	  evershop:
81	    image: evershop/evershop:2.2.1
82	    restart: unless-stopped
83	    environment:

# Self-host EverShop on redu

A real storefront with a real admin: catalogue, cart, checkout and orders, on one VM with a managed
Postgres beside it and a public HTTPS URL. About GBP 33 a month.

## What this deploys

- **EverShop** from the official image, pinned to `2.2.1`, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM: the catalogue, the orders and the customers.
- A volume on `/app/media`, which holds every product image you upload.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy EverShop on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The unusual thing about EverShop, and it is the important one

**Nobody can claim your store by finding the URL.** EverShop has no admin signup page at all. The
only admin routes are the login page and the login endpoint, and everything else under `/admin`
redirects an unauthenticated visitor straight back to the login form.

**The flip side is that a fresh deploy has no administrator whatsoever**, and no browser flow will
give you one. The admin account is created by a command inside the container, and until you run it
your shop has an open storefront and a locked back office you cannot enter.

Worse, **the command exits 0 whether or not it worked**: its error handler prints the error and
then exits successfully. So the recipe below creates the account and then proves it by logging in.

## The compose file

One service. redu supplies the database.

```yaml
services:
  evershop:
    image: evershop/evershop:2.2.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DB_HOST: ${PGHOST}
      DB_PORT: ${PGPORT}
      DB_NAME: ${PGDATABASE}
      DB_USER: ${PGUSER}
      DB_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
      EVERSHOP_HOME_URL: https://evershop-REPLACEME.redu.cloud
      PORT: "3000"
    volumes:
      - ./config:/app/config:ro
      - media:/app/media
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
volumes:
  media:
```

`DB_SSLMODE` is deliberately absent: unset means no TLS to a database that is only reachable on
the private network, and EverShop's `require` would demand a verifiable certificate. Use
`no-verify` if you want the connection encrypted anyway.

## The config file, which is where the session secret lives

`config/default.json`, mounted read-only at `/app/config`. Without it EverShop signs its cookies
with the string `keyboard cat`, which is upstream's documented example value.

```bash
mkdir -p config
SECRET=«REDACTED:assigned:a2abe951» -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9')
printf '{"system":{"session":{"cookieSecret":"%s"}}}\n' "$SECRET" > config/default.json
echo "keep this file: changing the secret signs out every admin and every customer"
```

Keep `config/default.json` for the next redeploy. The sessions themselves are rows in the managed
Postgres and survive; the signature on the cookie does not.

## Creating the administrator, and proving it

Run this once the storefront answers 200. The password goes into the container's argument list for
the moment the command runs, which is a limitation of the upstream CLI, so use a throwaway value
here and change it in the admin UI if that matters to you.

```bash
set -eu
HOST="$1"                      # evershop-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
EMAIL="$2"                     # the shop owner's email
# password on stdin, never in this script's own argument list
printf 'admin password: ' >&2
read -r PASSWORD

C=$(sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i evershop | head -1)
[ -n "$C" ] || { echo "no evershop container found; nothing to do" >&2; exit 3; }

# NOTE: this command exits 0 even when it fails. The login below is the real test.
sudo docker exec "$C" npm run user:create -- \
  --name "Store Owner" --email "$EMAIL" --password "$PASSWORD" || true

body=$(mktemp)
code=$(printf '{"email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$EMAIL" "$PASSWORD" \
  | curl -sS -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
      "https://$HOST/admin/user/login")

if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the edge, the container is still starting. Re-run in a minute." >&2
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" = "429" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: rate limited (8 login attempts per 15 minutes). Wait, then re-run." >&2
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: admin login returned $code. The account was NOT created." >&2
  cat "$body" >&2
  exit 1
fi
grep -q '"sid"' "$body" || {
  echo "FAIL: 200 but no session id in the body; this is not EverShop's login endpoint." >&2
  exit 3
}
echo "OK: the admin account exists, the password works, and the app reached the managed Postgres."

# The negative half. It only means something because the positive half above just passed.
adm=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin")
if [ "$adm" != "302" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous GET /admin returned $adm, expected a 302 to /admin/login." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the back office redirects an anonymous visitor to the login form."
```

## The three that actually break it

**`DB_SSLMODE=require` is not libpq's `require`.** In EverShop it turns certificate verification

redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/evershopcommerce/evershop
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: evershop/evershop:2.2.1
  port: 3000
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: evershop
quirks:
  - "PULL THE PINNED IMAGE, DO NOT BUILD. evershop/evershop:2.2.1 on Docker Hub, published 2026-08-12 and the newest release. The registry also carries latest and next; never write either into a recipe. Note the repo has TWO Dockerfiles and they are not interchangeable: docker/Dockerfile builds the published image by installing the released npm package, and the root Dockerfile builds the monorepo from source for contributors and is never published. You want neither, because the image already exists."
  - "⛔⛔ NOBODY BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR BY VISITING THE SITE, AND THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS. EverShop has NO admin signup route: the only admin pages in v2.2.1 are the login page, the login endpoint and the logout endpoint, and modules/auth/pages/admin/all/[context]auth.js redirects every other admin request straight to /admin/login when the session has no matching admin_user row. So an anonymous stranger CANNOT claim your store, which is unusual and good. The corollary is the part that bites: a fresh deploy has NO administrator at all and no way to create one from a browser. The admin account is created by a CLI call inside the container, at deploy time, and until you make it the shop has no owner. Do it as the last step of the deploy, before you hand over the URL."
  - "⛔ THE ADMIN-CREATION COMMAND EXITS 0 EVEN WHEN IT FAILED. bin/user/create.js catches every error and then calls process.exit(0), so a wrong password length, an unreachable database or a missing table all end in a green shell. NEVER treat the exit code as proof. Prove the outcome instead: POST the credentials to /admin/user/login and require HTTP 200 with a session id in the body. The verification script in this file does exactly that, and it is safe by construction because a 502 from the edge fails the login first."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST REACHES, BEFORE AND AFTER YOU CREATE THE ADMIN: the whole storefront, on purpose, because it is a shop. That includes GET / , the catalogue, the cart and the checkout, plus POST /api/customers, which is marked \"access\": \"public\" and is CUSTOMER registration, open by design and not admin registration. Everything under /admin is closed to anonymous requests, and every other /api route is private unless its own route.json says public (modules/auth/api/global/[getCurrentUser]auth.ts). Customer signup stays open after the first customer; there is no setting in v2.2.1 that closes it, so if the user needs a private store, put it behind something else rather than expecting a toggle."
  - "⛔ DATABASE: EverShop reads DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD as five separate variables (lib/postgres/connection.ts:9-14) and does NOT read a DATABASE_URL. deploy_compose only APPENDS redu's variables to the project .env, it never edits your compose, so the compose must map them itself: DB_HOST: ${PGHOST}, DB_PORT: ${PGPORT}, DB_NAME: ${PGDATABASE}, DB_USER: ${PGUSER}, DB_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}. There is NO SQLite fallback anywhere in the tree, so unlike most apps in this library a mis-wired database is loud rather than silent: the container fails on the first query. EverShop wants exactly ONE database, so redu's one-database-per-managed-server rule is satisfied and db_superuser is not needed."
  - "⛔ DB_SSLMODE MEANS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT libpq USERS EXPECT. In lib/postgres/connection.ts:18-56, require, prefer, verify-ca and verify-full all set rejectUnauthorized TRUE, i.e. the certificate IS verified, which is not what require means in libpq and is not what redu's managed Postgres presents. Leaving DB_SSLMODE unset gives ssl:false, which is the right answer over redu's private network: the app VM and the database VM are on the same private network and the database is not internet-reachable. If the user wants the connection encrypted anyway, the value is no-verify, NOT require. Say in the handover which one you chose."
  - "⛔ THE SESSION COOKIE SECRET DEFAULTS TO A PUBLICLY DOCUMENTED CONSTANT. getCookieSecret() returns the literal string \"keyboard cat\" when nothing is configured, and upstream's own configExample.text ships that same value, so every EverShop on the internet that skipped this step signs its session and cookie-parser cookies with a secret anyone can read. It is NOT an environment variable: it is the node-config key system.session.cookieSecret, so write it into a config file and mount it (this file shows how). Generate it once, keep it, and REUSE IT ON EVERY REDEPLOY: changing it signs out every admin and every logged-in customer at once. The session rows themselves live in the managed Postgres and survive."
  - "SET EVERSHOP_HOME_URL TO THE PUBLIC HTTPS URL, AND GENERATE THE DNAME YOURSELF UP FRONT. lib/util/getBaseUrl.ts falls back to http://localhost:3000, which then appears in emails, absolute links and the sitemap. The value must be known before the container starts, so generate the full evershop-<8 lowercase alphanumeric>.redu.cloud name yourself, pass it as the dname, and set EVERSHOP_HOME_URL to https:// plus that name. ⚠️ A value that is not a valid absolute http(s) URL THROWS during bootstrap and halts boot (assertValidHomeUrlEnv), so a typo here is a container that never starts, not a cosmetic bug."
  - "MOUNT A VOLUME ON /app/media OR EVERY PRODUCT IMAGE IS LOST ON THE NEXT REDEPLOY. lib/helpers.ts resolves MEDIAPATH to <cwd>/media and the image's working directory is /app, so uploads land on the container filesystem by default. The managed Postgres holds the catalogue, the orders and the customers; the image files attached to them are ordinary files on disk. This is the one people get wrong AFTER wiring the database correctly."
  - "DO NOT RUN `evershop install`, AND DO NOT LOOK FOR A MIGRATE STEP. bin/install/index.js:22-31 refuses to run when DB_HOST is set and prints \"look like you have already installed the system\"; its own comment says docker users should set environment variables and run start instead. Schema creation is not a separate step: bin/lib/startUp.js:50-56 runs every module migration on every start, inside a transaction, so the first boot creates the tables and later boots are a no-op."
  - "⛔ THERE IS NO /health ENDPOINT. modules/base/services/rateLimit.ts exempts /health and /healthz from rate limiting, which looks like a promise, but nothing in the tree registers either route: a container healthcheck pointed at one gets a 404 forever. Probe GET / instead, which is the storefront homepage and returns 200 with no products in the catalogue."
  - "RATE LIMITS ARE HARDCODED AND WILL BITE A RETRY LOOP. modules/base/services/rateLimit.ts: 300 page requests per minute per IP, 120 on /api, and only 8 per 15 minutes on the credential endpoints, which includes POST /admin/user/login. A verification script that retries the login in a poll loop locks itself out for a quarter of an hour and the 429 reads like a wrong password. Poll GET / until it answers 200, THEN attempt the login once. Leave TRUST_PROXY_HOPS at its default of 1, which is exactly right behind redu's single reverse proxy; raising it lets a client spoof X-Forwarded-For past the limiter."
  - "DELETE THE BUNDLED DATABASE FROM THE UPSTREAM COMPOSE. The repo's root docker-compose.yml runs a postgres:16 alongside the app with a password written into the file and 5432 published to the host, and pins the app to :latest. Use the one-service compose in this file instead: redu provides the database as its own private VM, and publishing 5432 on a VM with a public IP is a database on the internet with a known password."
  - "SIZING IS AN ESTIMATE AND UPSTREAM PUBLISHES NO NUMBER. The container runs THREE node processes, not one: bin/lib/startUp.js spawns a subscriber child and a cron child beside the web server, and both the storefront and the admin are server-rendered React. m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) is the reasoned floor for that; m1.small is likely to be tight. Measure it on the first real run and write the number back, because nothing upstream states one."
  - "OPTIONAL SAMPLE DATA, WITH A CAVEAT. The image ships `npm run seed`, which takes flags such as --categories --products --pages and fills an empty shop so you can see it working. # Self-host EverShop on redu

A real storefront with a real admin: catalogue, cart, checkout and orders, on one VM with a managed
Postgres beside it and a public HTTPS URL. About GBP 33 a month.

## What this deploys

- **EverShop** from the official image, pinned to `2.2.1`, on one m1.medium VM, port 3000.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM: the catalogue, the orders and the customers.
- A volume on `/app/media`, which holds every product image you upload.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.045/hour. Inside the no-card free trial. Delete it any time.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy EverShop on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The unusual thing about EverShop, and it is the important one

**Nobody can claim your store by finding the URL.** EverShop has no admin signup page at all. The
only admin routes are the login page and the login endpoint, and everything else under `/admin`
redirects an unauthenticated visitor straight back to the login form.

**The flip side is that a fresh deploy has no administrator whatsoever**, and no browser flow will
give you one. The admin account is created by a command inside the container, and until you run it
your shop has an open storefront and a locked back office you cannot enter.

Worse, **the command exits 0 whether or not it worked**: its error handler prints the error and
then exits successfully. So the recipe below creates the account and then proves it by logging in.

## The compose file

One service. redu supplies the database.

```yaml
services:
  evershop:
    image: evershop/evershop:2.2.1
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      DB_HOST: ${PGHOST}
      DB_PORT: ${PGPORT}
      DB_NAME: ${PGDATABASE}
      DB_USER: ${PGUSER}
      DB_PASSWORD: [REDACTED:value]}
      EVERSHOP_HOME_URL: https://evershop-REPLACEME.redu.cloud
      PORT: "3000"
    volumes:
      - ./config:/app/config:ro
      - media:/app/media
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
volumes:
  media:
```

`DB_SSLMODE` is deliberately absent: unset means no TLS to a database that is only reachable on
the private network, and EverShop's `require` would demand a verifiable certificate. Use
`no-verify` if you want the connection encrypted anyway.

## The config file, which is where the session secret lives

`config/default.json`, mounted read-only at `/app/config`. Without it EverShop signs its cookies
with the string `keyboard cat`, which is upstream's documented example value.

```bash
mkdir -p config
SECRET=«REDACTED:assigned:a2abe951» -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9')
printf '{"system":{"session":{"cookieSecret":"%s"}}}\n' "$SECRET" > config/default.json
echo "keep this file: changing the secret signs out every admin and every customer"
```

Keep `config/default.json` for the next redeploy. The sessions themselves are rows in the managed
Postgres and survive; the signature on the cookie does not.

## Creating the administrator, and proving it

Run this once the storefront answers 200. The password goes into the container's argument list for
the moment the command runs, which is a limitation of the upstream CLI, so use a throwaway value
here and change it in the admin UI if that matters to you.

```bash
set -eu
HOST="$1"                      # evershop-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
EMAIL="$2"                     # the shop owner's email
# password on stdin, never in this script's own argument list
printf 'admin password: ' >&2
read -r PASSWORD

C=$(sudo docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -i evershop | head -1)
[ -n "$C" ] || { echo "no evershop container found; nothing to do" >&2; exit 3; }

# NOTE: this command exits 0 even when it fails. The login below is the real test.
sudo docker exec "$C" npm run user:create -- \
  --name "Store Owner" --email "$EMAIL" --password "$PASSWORD" || true

body=$(mktemp)
code=$(printf '{"email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$EMAIL" "$PASSWORD" \
  | curl -sS -o "$body" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
      "https://$HOST/admin/user/login")

if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the edge, the container is still starting. Re-run in a minute." >&2
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" = "429" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: rate limited (8 login attempts per 15 minutes). Wait, then re-run." >&2
  exit 3
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: admin login returned $code. The account was NOT created." >&2
  cat "$body" >&2
  exit 1
fi
grep -q '"sid"' "$body" || {
  echo "FAIL: 200 but no session id in the body; this is not EverShop's login endpoint." >&2
  exit 3
}
echo "OK: the admin account exists, the password works, and the app reached the managed Postgres."

# The negative half. It only means something because the positive half above just passed.
adm=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/admin")
if [ "$adm" != "302" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: anonymous GET /admin returned $adm, expected a 302 to /admin/login." >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "OK: the back office redirects an anonymous visitor to the login form."
```

## The three that actually break it

**No admin exists until you make one**, and the command that makes one cannot fail visibly. Create
it as part of the deploy and prove it with a login.

**`DB_SSLMODE=require` is not libpq's `require`.** In EverShop it turns certificate verification
ON. Leave it unset on redu's private network.

**`/app/media` needs a volume.** Postgres holds the catalogue; the product images are files on
disk and disappear with the VM.

The deploy failed — but not on anything in the recipe. It failed in redu's provisioning step:

```
PROVISIONING FAILED at activity doMakeInstancePublic:
No MAC address found for the instance's networks.
```

That's the platform failing to attach a floating IP. The managed Postgres (#144) landed in `error` too with no VM behind it, and a *different* account's database created in the same minute (`docspell`, #146) failed identically — so this was a transient networking fault at 21:27, not the compose file, the image, or the DB wiring. Second attempt failed the same way, and I've found what's actually wrong. Stopping here rather than burning the last of your quota.

## What happened

Both attempts died at the same redu-side step:

```
PROVISIONING FAILED at activity doMakeInstancePublic:
No MAC address found for the instance's networks.
```

The underlying cause is visible in `list_volumes`: **two volumes have been stuck in `status: creating` since 21:27** — a 40 GB and a 20 GB, exactly the app VM and the Postgres VM of the first attempt. They never finished being created, so no instance was ever built, so there was no network port to make public. The MAC error is the downstream symptom, not the cause.

Evidence this is the platform and not the recipe:
- `db-donetick` provisioned fine at 21:27 while `db-evershop` failed in the same second — and `db-docspell` (not mine) failed identically. It's intermittent across the whole storage/network path.
- Nothing reached the point of pulling the image or reading the compose file. The compose, the `PG*` → `DB_*` mapping, the mounted session secret and `EVERSHOP_HOME_URL` were never exercised.

## Current state — nothing is running, nothing is billing

| Thing | State |
|---|---|
| Deployment 453 (attempt 1) | deleted by me |
| Deployment 456 (attempt 2) | gone from the API — no VM was ever created |
| Managed Postgres #144, #147 | `error`, no VM behind either, no data |
| Volumes (60 GB) from attempt 1 | **stuck in `creating`**, consuming 2 of your 10 volume slots |
| `https://evershop-jv2qk1d7.redu.cloud` | no TLS cert — the hostname was never provisioned |

Your local files are ready and correct: `docker-compose.yml`, `config/default.json` (keep this — it's the session secret), `redu-deploy-plan.md`.

## Why I stopped

**Volume quota is at 8/10, and one deploy needs exactly 2.** A third attempt would use your last two slots; if it fails the same way, those get stuck too and the account can't deploy anything at all until someone clears them by hand. That's a worse position than the one you're in now.

Two things I couldn't do myself:
- `delete_database(144)` was **blocked by the permission classifier**, so the two failed DB records are still there. They have no VM, so I don't believe they're billing, but I can't remove them without you allowing that call.
- The stuck volumes are in `creating`, which normally can't be deleted through the API anyway.

## How you'd like to proceed?

1. **Retry once now** — plausible, since the fault is intermittent, but it spends the last 2 volume slots.
2. **Wait ~15–30 min** for the storage backend to drain, then retry. My recommendation.
3. **Clear the wreckage first** — you allow `delete_database`, and redu support clears the two stuck volumes, then retry with room to spare.

Say which, and I'll pick it straight up — the upload, the plan and the admin-creation step are all ready to go.
